title: Work and power
when: Energy transferred by a force over a distance; power = energy per second (1 W = 1 J/s).

title: Photon energy
when: Energy of one photon from its frequency or wavelength. Use λ in metres for joules; E[eV] ≈ 1240/λ[nm].
note: The sheet gives E = hν; hc/λ follows with ν = c/λ.

title: Wavelength, frequency and refractive index
when: Wavelength inside a medium with index n; frequency stays the same, wavelength shrinks by n.

title: Planck’s law (spectral radiance)
when: Shape of a blackbody spectrum. Not needed numerically; know what it describes.
note: Lecture 1 slide 53 shows the per-frequency form B(ν, T).

title: Stefan–Boltzmann law
when: Total power per m² emitted by a blackbody at absolute temperature T (in K).

title: Wien’s displacement law
when: Peak wavelength of a blackbody spectrum.

title: Air mass
when: Relative path length through the atmosphere; θ is measured from the zenith.

title: Irradiance from a spectrum
when: Total power per m² = area under the spectral irradiance curve. Lecture writes P(λ) for I_eλ.

title: Irradiation
when: Energy per m² received over a period (J/m² or kWh/m²).

title: Spectral photon flux
when: Convert a power spectrum into a photon-number spectrum (divide by the photon energy at each λ). Lecture: Φ(λ) = P(λ)λ/hc.

title: Photon flux of monochromatic light
when: One wavelength (LED, laser): photons per m² per s = irradiance / energy per photon.

title: Absorption edge
when: Longest wavelength a semiconductor with bandgap E_G can absorb (c-Si: ≈ 1107 nm).

title: Photocurrent density from absorbed photons
when: One collected electron per absorbed photon. 1 A/m² = 0.1 mA/cm².

title: Snell’s law
when: Direction of the refracted ray. n sin θ is conserved through parallel layers.

title: Critical angle
when: Light inside the denser medium (n₂) hitting the surface beyond θcrit is totally reflected. Here n₁ < n₂.

title: Fresnel: s-polarised amplitude
when: Reflected amplitude ratio for s (perpendicular) polarisation. Get θt from Snell first.

title: Fresnel: p-polarised amplitude
when: Reflected amplitude ratio for p (parallel) polarisation.

title: Reflectance of unpolarised light
when: Sunlight is unpolarised: average the s and p reflectances (squares of the amplitudes).

title: Reflectance at normal incidence
when: θ = 0°: the quickest way to a reflectance. Used in every instruction-1 question at 0°.
note: Not on the sheet, but it follows from 4.12b/4.13b with all cosines = 1. Memorise it.

title: Path length through a layer
when: Distance a ray at internal angle θt travels to cross a layer of thickness d.

title: Best single-layer coating index
when: Interlayer index that minimises reflection without interference; here n₁ is the coating, n₀ the outside medium, nₛ the absorber.

title: Coating without interference (instruction method)
when: R₁ = air/coating, R₂ = coating/absorber, both at normal incidence; no multiple reflections or interference.
note: The book quotes 1 − (1 − R₁)(1 − R₂) instead; use the instruction method for Q1-type questions.

title: Quarter-wave coating
when: Coating thickness for destructive interference of the two reflections at λ₀: d = λ₀/(4n₁).

title: Complex refractive index
when: Optical constants of an absorbing material: n for speed/reflection, κ for absorption.
note: Book ex. 7.5 writes ñ = n − ik: same physics.

title: Absorption coefficient
when: From extinction coefficient to absorption coefficient; λ₀ = vacuum wavelength.

title: Lambert–Beer law
when: Intensity remaining at depth z in an absorbing layer.

title: Absorptance of a layer
when: Fraction absorbed in thickness t (single pass, ignoring reflection). Two passes: replace t by 2t.

title: Penetration depth
when: Depth where the intensity has dropped to 1/e ≈ 37 %.
